title: Static versus dynamic universality in the site-diluted kagome Ising model
authors: Alexandros Vasilopoulos, Zeynep Demir Vatansever, Erol Vatansever, Gerard T. Barkema, Nikolaos G. Fytas
abstract: We study the site-diluted Ising model on the kagome lattice using the Wolff single-cluster algorithm, focusing on both equilibrium and dynamic critical properties. The equilibrium critical exponents $ν= 1$ and $γ/ν= 7/4$ retain their exact pure Ising values for all spin concentrations $p$ considered, consistent with the marginal irrelevance of disorder at $α= 0$, with the specific heat crossing over from logarithmic to double-logarithmic growth upon dilution. These static results are shared between the kagome and square lattices. On the dynamic side, $z$ decreases upon dilution on both lattice, opposite to what is observed under local dynamics, with evidence of saturation to a $p$-independent value at strong dilution, suggesting a diluted dynamic fixed point. While $z$ is consistent between the two lattices in the pure case, it differs in the diluted regime, an effect we attribute to the two lattices sitting at different positions along the renormalization-group flow between the Ising and percolation fixed points, rather than to a true asymptotic breakdown of dynamic universality.
summary: This paper examines the critical behavior of the site-diluted Ising model on the kagome lattice, comparing static and dynamic universality. While static exponents remain robustly fixed to pure Ising values, the dynamic exponent $z$ shows lattice-dependent deviations in the diluted regime. The authors argue these differences stem from finite-size crossovers rather than a failure of dynamic universality.
main_problem: The study investigates the difference between static and dynamic universality classes in the site-diluted Ising model on the kagome lattice, comparing its behavior to the square lattice.
main_result: Static critical exponents retain their pure Ising values across all dilutions, while the dynamic exponent $z$ differs between the two lattices in the diluted regime, attributed to finite-size crossover effects rather than a breakdown of dynamic universality.
method: The research employs Monte Carlo simulations using the Wolff single-cluster algorithm to calculate equilibrium and dynamic critical properties.
model_or_system: The system is the site-diluted Ising model defined by the Hamiltonian $H = -\sum_{\langle ij angle} \epsilon_i \epsilon_j \sigma_i \sigma_j$ on the kagome lattice. The dilution is controlled by the spin concentration $p$.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the difference in $z$ between lattices in the diluted regime is due to finite-size crossover effects related to different percolation thresholds, not a fundamental breakdown of dynamic universality.

It then moves to dynamic properties, comparing the behavior of the dynamic exponent $z$ on the kagome and square lattices as a function of dilution $p$, concluding with an RG flow interpretation.
why_interesting: The comparison of dynamic critical exponents across different lattices and the identification of crossover effects versus true universality breakdown are fundamental questions in critical phenomena, relevant to understanding complex many-body dynamics.

FIG. 3. (a) Finite-size scaling of the magnetic susceptibil- ity peaks χ∗for the site-diluted Ising model on the kagome lattice, for all values of the spin concentration p consid- ered. The solid lines represent fits to the power-law ansatz χ∗∼Lγ/ν, with the extracted exponent ratios γ/ν consis- tent with the exact Ising value 7/4 for all p (see Table II). (b) Finite-size scaling of the specific heat peak C∗on the kagome lattice. The main panel shows the double-logarithmic scaling C∗∼log[log(L)] observed for the site-diluted cases (p < 1), while the inset demonstrates the logarithmic scaling C∗∼log(L) expected for the pure (p = 1) Ising universality class.

Scaling of the normalized average Wolff cluster size S/(pN) with system size L for the site-diluted Ising model on the kagome (a) and square (b) lattices, for all values of the spin concentration p considered. Solid lines are power- law fits of the form S ∼Lγ/ν, yielding exponent ratios that average to γ/ν = 1.747(4) across all dilutions. Both axes are on a logarithmic scale, with the power-law scaling appearing as straight lines.
